article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Evening Brief
article.dek: McCarthy practiced in full, the Giants moved to -2.5, rain is forecast at MetLife on Thursday — and the app board still shows last week's cards.

items.headline: Lead: McCarthy practiced in full — Thursday's quarterback question is answered, and rain is coming to MetLife
paragraphs: The one name hanging over Thursday night is settled, as far as it can be on a Tuesday. J.J. McCarthy practiced in full today with the hip pointer he picked up Sunday in Philadelphia, and he is expected to start against Washington on Thursday night barring a setback. Cam Skattebo is expected to be full-go too, after missing Week 9. The Giants are as healthy as they are going to get on a short week.

The other Thursday fact is the sky. The National Weather Service calls for rain at MetLife on Thursday, mainly after 1 p.m., with an 80% chance of precipitation into the night and wind gusting to 20 mph. Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET. That is the forecast as it stands — it gets a final check on Thursday, when it is actually useful.

One more result from Monday night, for the record: Buffalo's 23-6 win over Minnesota closed Week 9. The Bills covered -3.5 and the total went well under 45.5. That game is settled — the numbers that matter now are Thursday's.
items.takeaway: McCarthy practiced in full and is expected to start Thursday, Skattebo is back, and rain is forecast at MetLife — Thursday's two big questions have answers, two days early.

items.headline: Injuries: Murray's hamstring is worse than the morning read, Watson is set to start, and two stars are done for a while
paragraphs: Minnesota's quarterback problem got worse today. Kyler Murray's hamstring injury is a Grade 2 strain, and the new reporting puts him out 3-4 weeks. That is a longer absence than the morning's week-to-week read, and a Week 10 return now looks unlikely. Carson Wentz started Monday night and the Vikings' offense managed 81 passing yards.

Cleveland's spot firmed up the other way. Deshaun Watson has cleared the concussion protocol and the Browns are planning for him to start Sunday against Houston, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Seattle's Drew Lock says he will play Sunday at Las Vegas despite the oblique injury and elbow tendinitis, with Sam Darnold ruled out. In Arizona, Gardner Minshew is still seeking medical opinions on his torn UCL, and rookie Carson Beck remains in line to start against the Rams.

Two more names, both bad news for their teams. Rams receiver Puka Nacua is likely headed to injured reserve with turf toe plus MCL and PCL sprains. Packers running back Josh Jacobs requires surgery. Cardinals receiver Michael Wilson is out for the season with a neck injury.
items.takeaway: Murray is likely out 3-4 weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Watson is set to start Sunday, Lock says he will play — and Nacua and Jacobs are out for a while.

items.headline: Weather: rain at MetLife on Thursday, and the forecast is now firm enough to plan around
paragraphs: Thursday night at MetLife Stadium is going to be wet. The National Weather Service forecast for East Rutherford calls for rain, mainly after 1 p.m., high near 60, east wind 6 to 10 mph with gusts as high as 20 mph, and an 80% chance of precipitation through the night. The kickoff-window read is 51 degrees with 11 mph wind, gusts to 23, and rain.

This is a forecast fact, not a betting edge. Rain does not pick a side or a total on its own. It is worth knowing because Thursday is outdoors, and because the forecast has firmed up since the morning — it was a two-days-out guess then, and it is a real plan-around-it forecast now. The final check comes Thursday.
items.takeaway: Rain is forecast at MetLife on Thursday night — 80% chance, wind gusting to 20 mph, kickoff around 51 degrees. A forecast fact, not a totals edge.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — eight days old now, so Thursday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the board twice tonight, a couple of minutes apart. It is the same board as this morning, byte for byte — generated November 2, still showing Week 8. The headline cards are from last Monday night's Bears-Seahawks game: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. The Seahawks moneyline is the example: the app gave Seattle a 56.1% chance to win, while the -175 price needs 63.6% to break even, so the expected value is negative. That is the point — Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the app's plus-EV play — the Bears +3, with the app at 50.6% against a market that priced Chicago at 46.5%, for a small positive edge.

The board has not picked up today's news either. It still lists Kyler Murray as Minnesota's expected starter — he is now likely out 3-4 weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and Carson Wentz started Monday night. It knows nothing about McCarthy practicing in full today. Until the board flips to Week 10, there is no card to read for Thursday, so use Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price for Commanders-Giants — the Giants are -2.5 and the total is 41.5 at DraftKings right now — and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override. Thursday game? Thursday check.
items.takeaway: The board is eight days old and still shows last week's Week 8 cards — it still lists Murray as Minnesota's starter and knows nothing about McCarthy — so Thursday's Commanders-Giants price goes through Check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets — the money and the crowd are two different numbers
paragraphs: When a sportsbook shows betting splits, it shows two numbers: handle and tickets. Handle is the share of the money bet on a side. Tickets is the share of the number of bets on a side. They sound like the same thing. They are not.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40% of the handle is. That means lots of small bets are on the favorite, while the bigger bets are going the other way. The crowd is on one side and the money is on the other. That split is what people are looking at when they talk about sharp money — and it only means something when the two numbers actually disagree.

The other way around matters too. If 70% of the tickets and 70% of the handle are both on the same side, that is not a split. That is just a popular side. A popular side can still win. It just does not tell you anything about who the bigger bettors like.
items.takeaway: Handle is the share of the money, tickets is the share of the bets — when they disagree, the crowd and the money are on different sides, and that is the only time a split is telling you something.

items.headline: Thursday's numbers moved both ways — Giants -1.5 to -2.5, total 44.5 down to 41.5
paragraphs: Thursday's line has moved since the morning brief, and it moved on the news. The Giants opened as 1.5-point home favorites. They are now -2.5 at DraftKings, with the total down from 44.5 to 41.5. The spread moved a point late Monday, once the McCarthy news firmed up. The total has dropped three points since opening.

The money is with the move, not against it. Reported DraftKings splits from Monday evening had 71% of spread tickets and 89% of the money on the Giants. Tickets and handle agree on New York, so this is not a public-vs-money split — it is a popular side that the money likes too. That is why there is no Fade tonight: a Fade needs the two numbers to disagree, and here they do not.

The app board has caught none of this. It still shows Week 8 prices from November 2 — I checked twice tonight and it is byte-identical to this morning's board — and there is no Commanders-Giants game on it at all. If your book's Thursday number looks different from -2.5 or 41.5, run it through Check and let the app judge your price, not last week's.

If your book's Thursday number looks different from -2.5 or 41.5, run it through Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Giants -1.5 to -2.5 and the total 44.5 to 41.5 since the morning — the money agrees with the tickets on New York, so there is no Fade, just a line that has already moved.

items.headline: Waiting already cost a point — if Check says bet your Thursday number, bet it now
paragraphs: Here is the cost of waiting, in plain numbers. The Giants were -1.5 this morning. They are -2.5 now. If you liked New York at -1.5 and waited for a better price, you did not get one — you got a worse one. Waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.

So the rule for tonight is simple. If your book has a Thursday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. The one thing that would have been worth waiting for — McCarthy's status — is answered: he practiced in full. The inactives come out about 90 minutes before kickoff on Thursday, and that is the last word if your bet needs a specific name in the lineup. But if your bet does not need a name, there is nothing left to wait for.
Thursday game? Thursday check. But tonight's check is worth doing too — while your number is still there.
items.takeaway: The Giants moved from -1.5 to -2.5 while people waited — if Check says bet on your Thursday number, bet it now; wait only if your bet needs a name the inactives have not confirmed yet.
